results.detail: blocker: The template `tpl-pydeseq2-two-group@1.0.0` does not answer this task. It tests one test level against one reference level (a pairwise Wald test). The task asks which genes change monotonically across three doses (0, 10, 100 nM). A trend needs either a dose-as-numeric model, or a check that the 10 nM and 100 nM effects have the same sign and are ordered. A single pairwise contrast, such as 100 vs 0, cannot show that, because it ignores the 10 nM group. A 10 vs 0 contrast plus a 100 vs 0 contrast would also not give one adjusted p-value for the dose effect per gene. The slots only take a group column and two levels, so I cannot change this from the slot values. I did not run the template, since its output would not meet the acceptance criterion (a per-gene dose effect with an adjusted p-value). Data checked: 2000 genes, 6 samples, 2 replicates per dose, batch crossed with dose (batch 1 and 2 in every dose group). A suitable step would be a DESeq2 or PyDESeq2 model `~ batch + dose` with dose as a numeric (or log-dose) term, or a likelihood-ratio test. With only 2 replicates per dose, power will be limited, and the monotonicity of the 10 nM effect would need to be checked separately.; no successful run of the template; no DE script of its own

input.content:
"""Hallmark ORA of treatment-responsive genes.
Design: treated vs control DE (DESeq2, T1S1). Unranked list -> ORA.
Choices that read the data: DE genes = padj<0.05 (up / down / all, tested separately);
background = all genes with non-NA padj and a symbol (the tested universe).
Gene sets: MSigDB Hallmark 2024.1 (human symbols), size filtered 15-500 within the background.
FDR: BH across the 50 sets within each list (up, down, all).
"""
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import hypergeom
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PADJ = 0.05
de = pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/work/de_results.csv").dropna(subset=["padj", "symbol"])
bg = set(de.symbol)
sets = {}
for l in open("/mnt/refs/msigdb/hallmark/h.all.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"):
    p = l.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    g = set(p[2:]) & bg
    if 15 <= len(g) <= 500:
        sets[p[0]] = g

lists = {
    "all": de[de.padj < PADJ].symbol,
    "up": de[(de.padj < PADJ) & (de.log2FoldChange > 0)].symbol,
    "down": de[(de.padj < PADJ) & (de.log2FoldChange < 0)].symbol,
}
rows = []
N = len(bg)
for name, s in lists.items():
    hits = set(s); n = len(hits); out = []
    for t, g in sets.items():
        ov = hits & g; k = len(ov); K = len(g)
        p = hypergeom.sf(k - 1, N, K, n)
        out.append(dict(term=t, source="MSigDB_Hallmark_2024.1", direction=name, size=K,
                        n_hits=n, overlap=k, fold_enrichment=(k / n) / (K / N) if n else np.nan,
                        p_value=p, genes=";".join(sorted(ov))))
    d = pd.DataFrame(out); d["fdr"] = multipletests(d.p_value, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    rows.append(d)
res = pd.concat(rows).sort_values(["direction", "p_value"])
res.to_csv("hallmark_ora_results.csv", index=False)
print({k: len(v) for k, v in lists.items()}, "background", N, "sets", len(sets))
print(res[res.fdr < 0.05][["direction", "term", "size", "overlap", "fold_enrichment", "fdr"]].to_string())

# dot plot: top sets per direction (up/down), union of top 10 by p
top = res[res.direction.isin(["up", "down"])]
keep = top[top.fdr < 0.05].term.unique()
if len(keep) == 0:
    keep = top.sort_values("p_value").term.unique()[:10]
keep = list(keep)[:20]
pl = top[top.term.isin(keep)].copy()
pl["mlog"] = -np.log10(pl.fdr.clip(lower=1e-300))
order = pl.groupby("term").p_value.min().sort_values(ascending=False).index
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 0.35 * len(order) + 2))
for i, dname in enumerate(["up", "down"]):
    q = pl[pl.direction == dname]
    sc = ax.scatter([i] * len(q), [list(order).index(t) for t in q.term], s=30 + 25 * q.overlap,
                    c=q.mlog, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=max(pl.mlog.max(), 1))
ax.set_yticks(range(len(order))); ax.set_yticklabels([o.replace("HALLMARK_", "") for o in order], fontsize=8)
ax.set_xticks([0, 1]); ax.set_xticklabels(["up", "down"]); ax.set_xlim(-.6, 1.6)
plt.colorbar(sc, label="-log10 FDR"); ax.set_title("Hallmark ORA (padj<0.05 DE genes)\nsize = overlap")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("hallmark_dotplot.png", dpi=200)

# Design: treated(T1-3) vs control(C1-3), n=3/group; batch (1/2) is balanced across groups -> design ~ batch + group.
# Scale: raw integer counts -> PyDESeq2. Filter (reads outcome-blind): >=10 counts in >=3 samples. Contrast: treated vs control.
# Thresholds: BH padj<0.05 (DESeq2 default); highlight |log2FC|>1 in the plot only.
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataset
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats
np.random.seed(0)
c=pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-counts/counts.tsv",sep="\t")
m=pd.read_csv("/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-meta/samples.csv").set_index("sample")
m["batch"]=m["batch"].astype(str)
sym=c.set_index("gene_id")["symbol"]
X=c.set_index("gene_id").drop(columns="symbol")[m.index].T
print("library sizes",X.sum(1).to_dict())
X=X.loc[:,(X>=10).sum()>=3]; print("genes kept",X.shape[1],"of",len(c))
dds=DeseqDataset(counts=X,metadata=m,design="~batch+group",refit_cooks=True); dds.deseq2()
ds=DeseqStats(dds,contrast=["group","treated","control"]); ds.summary()
r=ds.results_df.reset_index().rename(columns={"index":"gene_id","log2FoldChange":"log2_fold_change","padj":"adjusted_p_value","pvalue":"p_value","baseMean":"base_mean"})
r.insert(1,"symbol",r.gene_id.map(sym)); r=r.sort_values("adjusted_p_value")
r.to_csv("results/de_treated_vs_control.csv",index=False)
s=r.adjusted_p_value<0.05
print("sig",s.sum(),"up",(s&(r.log2_fold_change>0)).sum(),"down",(s&(r.log2_fold_change<0)).sum(),"sig&|lfc|>1",(s&(r.log2_fold_change.abs()>1)).sum())
y=-np.log10(r.adjusted_p_value.clip(lower=1e-300)); big=s&(r.log2_fold_change.abs()>1)
plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.scatter(r.log2_fold_change,y,s=6,c="lightgrey")
plt.scatter(r.log2_fold_change[big],y[big],s=8,c=np.where(r.log2_fold_change[big]>0,"firebrick","royalblue"))
plt.axhline(-np.log10(.05),ls="--",c="k",lw=.5);[plt.axvline(v,ls="--",c="k",lw=.5) for v in(-1,1)]
for _,t in r.head(8).iterrows(): plt.annotate(t.symbol,(t.log2_fold_change,-np.log10(max(t.adjusted_p_value,1e-300))),fontsize=6)
plt.xlabel("log2 fold change (treated vs control)");plt.ylabel("-log10 adjusted p");plt.title("Treated vs control");plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("figures/volcano.png",dpi=200)
